style.vernacular: Abandoned Norwegian-founded whaling settlement (1904-1965) at the head of King Edward Cove, South Georgia: small utilitarian timber and corrugated-iron buildings, rust-red and weathered, with a white timber church and a white manager's villa, set on a flat tussock-grass shelf below snowy mountains, with rusting tanks, ships and whale-processing plant on the shore.
style.ornament: Almost none: functional Norwegian industrial vernacular. Neo-Gothic carved timber trim and a roof turret on the church, verandah and hip roof on the villa; exposed rust, whale bones, harpoon guns and ship hulks as set dressing.

sources.what: sheltered flat area at head of King Edward Cove, derelict station with rusting plants and ships, church 1913, museum in manager's house, tundra climate
neo-Gothic 1913 prefabricated church, single nave, white interior
